note: The spider from the 1st fret, where the frets are widest: one finger per fret on every string, followed from the tab with the finger row under it. Only the tempo moves (60 to 80 bpm); the way through the strings is spelled out, and the goal names muscle memory.

exercise.title: Spider from the 1st fret
exercise.why: Low on the neck the frets are widest, so one finger per fret there stretches the hand further than anywhere else, and every shape higher up feels smaller after it.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}, and follow the tab. Play frets 1 to 4 with fingers 1, 2, 3 and 4 on the low E string, then on each string in turn up to the high e string, and come back down the same way, one note per beat.
Practice until the order is in your muscle memory: each finger lands on its own fret without you looking.
